source.text: וַיַּ֥עַל דָּוִ֖ד מִשָּׁ֑ם וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בִּמְצָד֥וֹת עֵֽין־גֶּֽדִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up David from there and stayed in [the] strongholds of En-gedi.

en.L: And David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-gedi.
en.B: David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-gedi.
en.R: David left that place and went to live in the safe places in the hills at En-gedi.

es.L: Y subió David de allí y se quedó en las fortalezas de En-gadi.
es.B: David subió de allí y se quedó en las fortalezas de En-gadi.
es.R: David se fue de aquel lugar y se fue a vivir en los lugares seguros de las colinas de En-gadi.

fr.L: Et David monta de là et demeura dans les forteresses d’En-Guédi.
fr.B: David monta de là et s’établit dans les forteresses d’En-Guédi.
fr.R: David a quitté cet endroit et il est allé vivre dans les endroits sûrs des collines, à En-Guédi.

sw.L: Daudi akapanda kutoka huko, akakaa katika ngome za En-gedi.
sw.B: Daudi akapanda kutoka huko, akakaa katika ngome za En-gedi.
sw.R: Daudi akaondoka mahali pale, akaenda kuishi katika maficho salama milimani huko En-gedi.

vi.L: Đa-vít đi lên từ đó và ở trong các đồn lũy Ên-ghê-đi.
vi.B: Đa-vít đi lên từ đó và ở trong các đồn lũy Ên-ghê-đi.
vi.R: Đa-vít rời nơi ấy và đến sống tại những nơi an toàn trong vùng đồi Ên-ghê-đi.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 그곳에서 올라가 엔게디의 요새들에 머물렀다.
ko.B: 다윗은 그곳에서 올라가 엔게디의 요새들에 머물렀다.
ko.R: 다윗은 그곳을 떠나 엔게디의 산속, 안전하게 숨을 수 있는 곳에서 지냈다.

pt.L: E Davi subiu dali e ficou nas fortalezas de En-Gedi.
pt.B: Davi subiu dali e ficou nas fortalezas de En-Gedi.
pt.R: Davi saiu daquele lugar e foi morar nos refúgios seguros dos montes de En-Gedi.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: in the Hebrew text this sentence is 24:1
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. There chapter 23 ends at verse 28, and this sentence is counted as the first verse of chapter 24. Many Bibles print it as 23:29 and begin chapter 24 with the next sentence, so every verse of this chapter is one number lower there: 24:2-23 here is 24:1-22 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the strongholds of En-gedi: hard-to-reach places in the hills by the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: En-gedi is a spring on the western shore of the Dead Sea, below steep cliffs full of caves (Joshua 15:62). "From there" is the wilderness of Maon, where Saul nearly caught David before a Philistine raid called him away (23:24-28). "Strongholds" are natural refuges in the rocks that a small band could hold, as in 23:14, 19.

decisions.choice: safe places in the hills
decisions.reason: Readable explains "strongholds" as places in the hills where David's band was safe, since the word here means natural refuges rather than built forts.

decisions.choice: En-Guédi
decisions.reason: A name not in the terms table, in its usual French form, kept the same through both books.

decisions.choice: En-gadi
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish form of the oasis by the Dead Sea (m2), kept through the chapter.

decisions.choice: "En-gedi"
decisions.reason: Names not in the terms note take a Swahili spelling and are kept through the block; the hyphen keeps the two parts of the name ("spring of the kid") visible, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Ên-ghê-đi"
decisions.reason: A name not in the terms note's table, in the usual Protestant form; kept the same through both books.

decisions.choice: "엔게디" for En-gedi
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Korean form of the name. The Hebrew verse numbering is kept, as the English record says; nothing in the wording changes.

decisions.choice: En-Gedi
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also verse 2): "En-Gedi", the form of Joshua 15:62 in Portuguese, the two parts joined by a hyphen and each capitalised. "Fortalezas" are natural refuges, as at 23:14; Readable explains them, as the English does.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁ֣ב שָׁא֔וּל מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד בְּמִדְבַּ֖ר עֵ֥ין גֶּֽדִי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was when returned Saul from after [the] Philistines, and they told him, saying, Look, David [is] in [the] wilderness of En-gedi.

en.L: And it happened, when Saul returned from [going] after the Philistines, that they told him, saying, "Look, David is in the wilderness of En-gedi."
en.B: When Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, word was brought to him: "David is in the wilderness of En-gedi."
en.R: Saul came back from fighting the Philistines. Then someone told him, "David is in the desert near En-gedi."

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando Saúl volvió de [perseguir] a los filisteos, le avisaron, diciendo: «He aquí que David [está] en el desierto de En-gadi».
es.B: Cuando Saúl regresó de perseguir a los filisteos, le llegó la noticia: «David está en el desierto de En-gadi».
es.R: Saúl volvió de pelear contra los filisteos. Entonces alguien le dijo: «David está en el desierto, cerca de En-gadi».

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand Saül revint de la poursuite des Philistins, qu’on le lui rapporta, en disant : « Voici, David [est] dans le désert d’En-Guédi. »
fr.B: Quand Saül revint de la poursuite des Philistins, on vint lui dire : « David est dans le désert d’En-Guédi. »
fr.R: Saül est revenu après avoir combattu les Philistins. Alors quelqu’un lui a dit : « David est dans le désert, près d’En-Guédi. »

sw.L: Ikawa Sauli aliporudi kutoka [kuwafuatia] Wafilisti, wakamwambia, wakisema, "Tazama, Daudi yuko katika nyika ya En-gedi."
sw.B: Sauli aliporudi kutoka kuwafuatia Wafilisti, akaletewa habari: "Daudi yuko katika nyika ya En-gedi."
sw.R: Sauli akarudi kutoka kupigana na Wafilisti. Kisha mtu mmoja akamwambia, "Daudi yuko jangwani karibu na En-gedi."

vi.L: Khi Sau-lơ trở về sau khi đuổi theo người Phi-li-tin, người ta báo cho ông rằng: "Kìa, Đa-vít đang ở trong hoang mạc Ên-ghê-đi."
vi.B: Khi Sau-lơ đuổi đánh người Phi-li-tin trở về, có người báo tin cho ông: "Đa-vít đang ở trong hoang mạc Ên-ghê-đi."
vi.R: Sau-lơ đánh người Phi-li-tin trở về. Bấy giờ có người báo cho ông: "Đa-vít đang ở trong vùng hoang mạc gần Ên-ghê-đi."

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 블레셋 사람들을 뒤쫓다가 돌아왔을 때, 사람들이 그에게 알려 말했다. "보십시오, 다윗이 엔게디 광야에 있습니다."
ko.B: 사울이 블레셋 사람들을 뒤쫓다가 돌아오자, 누군가가 그에게 알렸다. "다윗이 엔게디 광야에 있습니다."
ko.R: 사울은 블레셋 사람들과 싸우고 돌아왔다. 그때 어떤 사람이 그에게 말했다. "다윗이 엔게디 근처 광야에 있습니다."

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando Saul voltou de [ir] atrás dos filisteus, lhe contaram, dizendo: "Eis que Davi está no deserto de En-Gedi."
pt.B: Quando Saul voltou da perseguição aos filisteus, recebeu a notícia: "Davi está no deserto de En-Gedi."
pt.R: Saul voltou da luta contra os filisteus. Então alguém lhe disse: "Davi está no deserto perto de En-Gedi."

decisions.choice: verse numbers: many Bibles begin chapter 24 here
decisions.reason: Because the Hebrew text counts the previous sentence as 24:1 (see the note there), this verse is 24:2 here and 24:1 in many Bibles. Every verse to the end of the chapter is one number higher here than there.

decisions.choice: returned from after the Philistines: the raid of 23:27-28
decisions.reason: Saul had broken off his hunt for David to meet a Philistine raid on the land (23:27-28). Once that was dealt with, he turned back to David.

decisions.choice: they told him: an unnamed report
decisions.reason: The verb is plural with no named subject: people told Saul. As in 23:19, local informers kept Saul aware of where David was.

decisions.choice: word was brought to him (Balanced); someone told him (Readable); desert near En-gedi (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid an unclear "they". The "wilderness" is dry, rocky country with little rain, so Readable says "desert".

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח שָׁא֗וּל שְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֛ים אִ֥ישׁ בָּח֖וּר מִכָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ לְבַקֵּ֤שׁ אֶת־דָּוִד֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו עַל־פְּנֵ֖י צוּרֵ֥י הַיְּעֵלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Saul three thousand men chosen from all Israel and went to seek David and his men on [the] face of [the] rocks of the wild goats.

en.L: And Saul took 3,000 chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men on the face of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
en.B: So Saul took 3,000 men chosen from all Israel and set out to search for David and his men east of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
en.R: So Saul took 3,000 of the best soldiers in all Israel. He went to look for David and his men near the cliffs called the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

es.L: Y tomó Saúl 3 000 hombres escogidos de todo Israel, y fue a buscar a David y a sus hombres frente a las Peñas de las Cabras Monteses.
es.B: Entonces Saúl tomó 3 000 hombres escogidos de todo Israel y salió a buscar a David y a sus hombres al este de las Peñas de las Cabras Monteses.
es.R: Entonces Saúl tomó a 3 000 de los mejores soldados de todo Israel. Fue a buscar a David y a sus hombres cerca de los acantilados llamados Peñas de las Cabras Monteses.

fr.L: Et Saül prit trois mille hommes d’élite de tout Israël, et il alla chercher David et ses hommes en face des Rochers des Bouquetins.
fr.B: Saül prit donc trois mille hommes choisis dans tout Israël et partit à la recherche de David et de ses hommes, à l’est des Rochers des Bouquetins.
fr.R: Alors Saül a pris trois mille des meilleurs soldats de tout Israël. Il est parti chercher David et ses hommes près des falaises qu’on appelle les Rochers des Bouquetins.

sw.L: Sauli akachukua watu 3,000 waliochaguliwa katika Israeli yote, akaenda kumtafuta Daudi na watu wake mbele ya Miamba ya Mbuzi-mwitu.
sw.B: Basi Sauli akachukua watu 3,000 waliochaguliwa katika Israeli yote, akaenda kumtafuta Daudi na watu wake upande wa mashariki wa Miamba ya Mbuzi-mwitu.
sw.R: Basi Sauli akachukua askari 3,000 walio bora kuliko wote katika Israeli. Akaenda kumtafuta Daudi na watu wake karibu na majabali yaitwayo Miamba ya Mbuzi-mwitu.

vi.L: Sau-lơ đem theo 3.000 người được chọn trong cả Y-sơ-ra-ên và đi tìm Đa-vít cùng những người của ông, trên mặt Các Tảng Đá Dê Rừng.
vi.B: Vậy Sau-lơ đem theo 3.000 người tuyển chọn trong cả Y-sơ-ra-ên và lên đường lùng tìm Đa-vít cùng thuộc hạ ở phía đông Các Tảng Đá Dê Rừng.
vi.R: Vậy Sau-lơ đem theo 3.000 người lính giỏi nhất trong cả Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ông đi tìm Đa-vít và thuộc hạ gần những vách đá gọi là Các Tảng Đá Dê Rừng.

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 온 이스라엘에서 뽑은 사람 삼천 명을 데리고, 들염소 바위 앞으로 다윗과 그의 부하들을 찾으러 갔다.
ko.B: 그래서 사울은 온 이스라엘에서 뽑은 군인 삼천 명을 거느리고, 들염소 바위 동쪽으로 다윗과 그의 부하들을 찾으러 나섰다.
ko.R: 그래서 사울은 온 이스라엘에서 가장 뛰어난 군인 삼천 명을 데리고 갔다. 그는 '들염소 바위'라고 부르는 절벽 근처로 다윗과 그의 부하들을 찾으러 갔다.

pt.L: E Saul tomou três mil homens escolhidos de todo o Israel e foi procurar Davi e os seus homens na face dos Rochedos das Cabras Monteses.
pt.B: Então Saul tomou três mil homens escolhidos de todo o Israel e partiu em busca de Davi e dos seus homens a leste dos Rochedos das Cabras Monteses.
pt.R: Então Saul pegou três mil dos melhores soldados de todo o Israel. Ele foi procurar Davi e os seus homens perto dos penhascos chamados Rochedos das Cabras Monteses.

decisions.choice: chosen men: picked fighting men
decisions.reason: These are soldiers selected for skill, as in 26:2 and Judges 20:15-16. Saul had already kept such a band of 3,000 near him (13:2). The number is far larger than David's six hundred (23:13).

decisions.choice: Rocks of the Wild Goats: probably a local name for the cliffs
alternatives: the rocks of the wild goats (a description)
decisions.reason: The ibex, a wild mountain goat, still lives among the cliffs at En-gedi. The phrase may be a place name or a description, "the rocks where the wild goats are"; the sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: on the face of: in front of, facing, or to the east of
alternatives: on the face of the cliffs
decisions.reason: The expression can mean "in front of" or, since a person facing the sunrise has the east before him, "east of". It places the search near those cliffs without saying exactly where.

decisions.choice: east of
decisions.reason: Balanced takes the expression in its common sense of direction; Readable says only "near", which keeps the less certain point open.
Numbers above ninety-nine are given in figures at every level.

decisions.choice: les Rochers des Bouquetins
decisions.reason: The wild goat of En-gedi is the ibex (m2), "bouquetin" in French; as a place name it takes capitals.

decisions.choice: trois mille
decisions.reason: The English writes numbers over ninety-nine in figures (r-en-2); the French style guide writes round numbers in words in running text, so "trois mille".

decisions.choice: las Peñas de las Cabras Monteses
alternatives: las Rocas de las Cabras Salvajes
decisions.reason: Probably a local name for the cliffs (m2), translated as the English translates it; “cabras monteses” is the Spanish name of the wild goat of the region.

decisions.choice: "Miamba ya Mbuzi-mwitu"
decisions.reason: "Mbuzi-mwitu" (wild goat) names the ibex of the En-gedi cliffs (m2); the name is kept in capitals as a place name, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Các Tảng Đá Dê Rừng"
decisions.reason: Probably a local name for the cliffs (m2), translated as the English translates it; numbers in figures follow the English, with the Vietnamese thousands point.

decisions.choice: "들염소 바위" for the Rocks of the Wild Goats
decisions.reason: A local name for the cliffs (meaning decision m2), translated rather than transliterated, as the English does.

decisions.choice: três mil
decisions.reason: For the whole book: round numbers are written in words in running text at every level (docs/portuguese-style.md section 5), as Judges 7:3 does in Portuguese, where the English uses figures above ninety-nine.

decisions.choice: os Rochedos das Cabras Monteses
decisions.reason: "Cabra montês" is the Portuguese name for the wild mountain goat, the ibex (m2); the phrase is capitalised as a place name, as the English does.

source.text: וַ֠יָּבֹא אֶל־גִּדְר֨וֹת הַצֹּ֤אן עַל־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ וְשָׁ֣ם מְעָרָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א שָׁא֖וּל לְהָסֵ֣ךְ אֶת־רַגְלָ֑יו וְדָוִד֙ וַאֲנָשָׁ֔יו בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמְּעָרָ֖ה יֹשְׁבִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he came to [the] sheepfolds of the flock by the road, and there [was] a cave, and went in Saul to cover his feet. And David and his men [were] in [the] innermost parts of the cave sitting.

en.L: And he came to the sheepfolds by the road, and a cave was there, and Saul went in to cover his feet. And David and his men were sitting in the innermost parts of the cave.
en.B: He came to the sheep pens along the road. A cave was there, and Saul went in to relieve himself, while David and his men sat far back in the cave.
en.R: He came to some sheep pens beside the road. There was a cave there, and Saul went into it to relieve himself. David and his men were sitting deep inside that same cave.

es.L: Y llegó a los rediles de ovejas junto al camino, y allí [había] una cueva, y entró Saúl a cubrir sus pies. Y David y sus hombres estaban sentados en lo más profundo de la cueva.
es.B: Llegó a unos corrales de ovejas junto al camino. Allí había una cueva, y Saúl entró a hacer sus necesidades, mientras David y sus hombres estaban sentados en el fondo de la cueva.
es.R: Llegó a unos corrales de ovejas que había junto al camino. Allí había una cueva, y Saúl entró en ella para hacer sus necesidades. David y sus hombres estaban sentados muy adentro de esa misma cueva.

fr.L: Et il arriva aux parcs à moutons près du chemin, et il y avait là une grotte, et Saül y entra pour se couvrir les pieds. Et David et ses hommes étaient assis au fond de la grotte.
fr.B: Il arriva aux enclos à moutons qui bordaient le chemin. Il y avait là une grotte, et Saül y entra pour se soulager, tandis que David et ses hommes étaient assis au fond de la grotte.
fr.R: Il est arrivé à des enclos à moutons au bord du chemin. Il y avait là une grotte, et Saül y est entré pour faire ses besoins. Or David et ses hommes étaient assis tout au fond de cette même grotte.

sw.L: Akafika kwenye mazizi ya kondoo kando ya njia, na pango lilikuwa huko, naye Sauli akaingia kufunika miguu yake. Daudi na watu wake walikuwa wameketi sehemu za ndani kabisa za pango.
sw.B: Akafika kwenye mazizi ya kondoo kando ya njia. Palikuwa na pango pale, naye Sauli akaingia kujisaidia, wakati Daudi na watu wake walikuwa wameketi ndani kabisa ya pango.
sw.R: Akafika kwenye mazizi ya kondoo kando ya njia. Palikuwa na pango pale, naye Sauli akaingia ndani yake kujisaidia. Daudi na watu wake walikuwa wameketi ndani kabisa ya pango hilo hilo.

vi.L: Ông đến các chuồng chiên bên đường, ở đó có một cái hang, và Sau-lơ vào đó để che chân mình. Đa-vít và những người của ông đang ngồi ở tận bên trong hang.
vi.B: Ông đến các chuồng chiên bên đường. Ở đó có một cái hang, và Sau-lơ vào trong để đi tiểu tiện, trong khi Đa-vít và thuộc hạ đang ngồi sâu trong hang.
vi.R: Ông đến mấy chuồng chiên bên đường. Ở đó có một cái hang, và Sau-lơ vào hang để đi vệ sinh. Đa-vít và thuộc hạ đang ngồi sâu bên trong chính cái hang ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 길가에 있는 양 우리에 이르렀는데, 그곳에 굴이 있었다. 사울이 발을 가리려고 들어갔다. 그때 다윗과 그의 부하들은 굴 안쪽 깊은 곳에 앉아 있었다.
ko.B: 사울은 길가에 있는 양 우리에 이르렀다. 그곳에 굴이 있었는데, 사울이 용변을 보려고 그 안으로 들어갔다. 그때 다윗과 그의 부하들은 굴 안쪽 깊숙한 곳에 앉아 있었다.
ko.R: 사울은 길가에 있는 양 우리 몇 곳에 이르렀다. 그곳에는 굴이 하나 있었는데, 사울은 용변을 보려고 그 굴에 들어갔다. 그런데 다윗과 그의 부하들이 바로 그 굴 깊숙한 곳에 앉아 있었다.

pt.L: E ele chegou aos currais de ovelhas junto ao caminho, e havia ali uma caverna, e Saul entrou para cobrir os pés. E Davi e os seus homens estavam sentados nas partes mais fundas da caverna.
pt.B: Ele chegou aos currais de ovelhas que ficavam junto ao caminho. Havia ali uma caverna, e Saul entrou nela para fazer as suas necessidades, enquanto Davi e os seus homens estavam sentados lá no fundo da caverna.
pt.R: Ele chegou a uns currais de ovelhas na beira do caminho. Ali havia uma caverna, e Saul entrou nela para fazer as suas necessidades. Davi e os seus homens estavam sentados bem no fundo daquela mesma caverna.

decisions.choice: to cover his feet: to relieve himself
decisions.reason: This is a polite way of speaking about going to the toilet: a man squatting in a long robe covered his feet with it. The same expression is used of King Eglon in Judges 3:24. One ancient translation took it to mean that Saul went in to get ready or to rest, but the expression is the one used in Judges, and the story needs Saul to be alone, off guard and close enough for David to reach him.

decisions.choice: sheepfolds: stone pens for the flocks
decisions.reason: Shepherds built low stone walls, often at a cave mouth, to keep their flocks safe at night. Caves in these hills were used as shelters for sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: innermost parts: the far back of the cave
decisions.reason: The word means the farthest or deepest part of something (Judges 19:1; Amos 6:10). David's band sat in the dark at the back while Saul came into the lit entrance.

decisions.choice: to relieve himself
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "to cover his feet"; Balanced and Readable give its meaning plainly, as at Judges 3:24, where the same words are used.

decisions.choice: hacer sus necesidades
decisions.reason: “To cover his feet” is a polite way of saying to relieve himself (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase; Balanced and Readable use the polite Spanish expression for the same thing, as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: "kufunika miguu yake" (L); "kujisaidia" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture (m1); Balanced and Readable use "kujisaidia", the usual polite Swahili word for relieving oneself.

decisions.choice: "che chân mình" (L); "đi tiểu tiện" (B); "đi vệ sinh" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's polite phrase; the other levels say what it means (m1), in words a public reading can bear.

decisions.choice: "용변을 보려고" (to relieve himself) at Balanced and Readable; Literal "발을 가리려고" (to cover his feet)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is a polite idiom (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps the picture, the other levels give the sense in an equally polite Korean phrase.

decisions.choice: cobrir os pés (L); fazer as suas necessidades (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Judges 3:24 in Portuguese for the same expression (m1): Literal keeps the picture, Balanced and Readable say "fazer as suas necessidades", the polite Portuguese phrase; "usar o banheiro" would be out of place in a cave.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י דָוִ֜ד אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה הַיּ֜וֹם אֲֽשֶׁר־אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֣ה אֵלֶ֗יךָ הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י נֹתֵ֤ן אֶת־אֹֽיִבְךָ֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר יִטַ֣ב בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וַיִּכְרֹ֛ת אֶת־כְּנַֽף־הַמְּעִ֥יל אֲשֶׁר־לְשָׁא֖וּל בַּלָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] men of David to him, Look, the day which said [the] LORD to you, Look, I [am] giving your enemy into your hand, and you will do to him as is good in your eyes. And arose David and cut off [the] corner of the robe which [belonged] to Saul in secret.

en.L: And the men of David said to him, "Look, [this is] the day of which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to you, 'Look, I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as is good in your eyes.'" And David arose and cut off the corner of the robe that belonged to Saul secretly.
en.B: David's men said to him, "This is the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke of when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you, 'I am going to give your enemy into your hand, and you may do to him whatever you think best.'" Then David got up and quietly cut off the corner of Saul's robe.
en.R: David's men whispered to him, "This is the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told you about! He said, 'I will hand your enemy over to you. You can do to him whatever you want.'" David got up and crept close. Without Saul noticing, he cut off a corner of Saul's robe.

es.L: Y le dijeron los hombres de David: «He aquí el día del cual {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te dijo: “He aquí que yo entrego a tu enemigo en tu mano, y harás con él como bien te parezca a tus ojos”». Y se levantó David y cortó en secreto la orilla del manto que era de Saúl.
es.B: Los hombres de David le dijeron: «Este es el día del que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te habló cuando te dijo: “Voy a entregar a tu enemigo en tu mano, y podrás hacer con él lo que mejor te parezca”». Entonces David se levantó y, sin hacer ruido, cortó la orilla del manto de Saúl.
es.R: Los hombres de David le dijeron en voz baja: «¡Este es el día del que te habló {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! Te dijo: “Voy a entregarte a tu enemigo. Podrás hacer con él lo que quieras”». David se levantó y se acercó sin hacer ruido. Sin que Saúl se diera cuenta, le cortó un pedazo de la orilla del manto.

fr.L: Et les hommes de David lui dirent : « Voici le jour dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a dit : “Voici, je livre ton ennemi dans ta main, et tu lui feras ce qui est bon à tes yeux.” » Et David se leva et coupa en secret le pan du manteau qui appartenait à Saül.
fr.B: Les hommes de David lui dirent : « C’est le jour dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} parlait quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} t’a dit : “Je vais livrer ton ennemi entre tes mains, et tu lui feras ce que tu jugeras bon.” » Alors David se leva et coupa sans bruit le pan du manteau de Saül.
fr.R: Les hommes de David lui ont dit tout bas : « C’est le jour dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a parlé ! Il t’a dit : “Je vais te livrer ton ennemi. Tu pourras lui faire tout ce que tu voudras.” » David s’est levé et s’est approché en silence. Sans que Saül s’en aperçoive, il a coupé un morceau du manteau de Saül.

sw.L: Watu wa Daudi wakamwambia, "Tazama, [hii ni] siku ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuambia, 'Tazama, ninamtia adui yako mkononi mwako, nawe utamtendea kama itakavyokuwa njema machoni pako.'" Daudi akainuka, akakata pindo la joho la Sauli kwa siri.
sw.B: Watu wa Daudi wakamwambia, "Hii ndiyo siku ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema habari zake alipokuambia, 'Nitamtia adui yako mikononi mwako, nawe utamtendea lolote unaloona kuwa jema.'" Ndipo Daudi akainuka, akakata kimya kimya pindo la joho la Sauli.
sw.R: Watu wa Daudi wakamnong'oneza, "Hii ndiyo siku ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuambia habari zake! Alisema, 'Nitamtia adui yako mikononi mwako. Unaweza kumtendea lolote unalotaka.'" Daudi akainuka, akasogea karibu. Bila Sauli kujua, akakata kipande cha pindo la joho lake.

vi.L: Những người của Đa-vít nói với ông: "Kìa, [đây là] ngày mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với ông: 'Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phó kẻ thù của ngươi vào tay ngươi, và ngươi sẽ làm cho nó điều gì ngươi thấy là tốt.'" Đa-vít đứng dậy, lén cắt vạt áo choàng của Sau-lơ.
vi.B: Thuộc hạ của Đa-vít nói với ông: "Đây là ngày {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã nói đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo ông: '{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phó kẻ thù của con vào tay con, và con muốn làm gì nó tùy ý.'" Bấy giờ Đa-vít đứng dậy, lặng lẽ cắt vạt áo choàng của Sau-lơ.
vi.R: Thuộc hạ của Đa-vít thì thầm với ông: "Đây là ngày {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã nói với ông! Ngài phán: '{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giao kẻ thù của con cho con. Con muốn làm gì nó cũng được.'" Đa-vít đứng dậy và rón rén đến gần. Không để Sau-lơ hay biết, ông cắt một vạt áo choàng của Sau-lơ.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗의 부하들이 그에게 말했다. "보십시오, 이날은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 장군님께 '보아라, 내가 네 원수를 네 손에 넘겨줄 것이니, 너는 네 눈에 좋은 대로 그에게 하여라' 하고 말씀하신 바로 그날입니다." 그러자 다윗이 일어나 사울의 겉옷 자락을 몰래 잘랐다.
ko.B: 다윗의 부하들이 그에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 '내가 네 원수를 네 손에 넘겨줄 것이니, 너는 좋을 대로 그에게 하여라' 하고 장군님께 말씀하신 날이 바로 오늘입니다." 그러자 다윗은 일어나서 사울의 겉옷 자락을 살그머니 잘랐다.
ko.R: 다윗의 부하들이 다윗에게 속삭였다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 장군님께 말씀하신 날이 바로 오늘입니다! 주님께서 '내가 네 원수를 너에게 넘겨주겠다. 너는 그에게 하고 싶은 대로 하여라' 하고 말씀하셨습니다." 다윗은 일어나 살금살금 다가갔다. 그리고 사울이 모르게 사울의 겉옷 자락을 잘랐다.

pt.L: E os homens de Davi lhe disseram: "Eis o dia de que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} falou ao senhor: 'Eis que eu entrego o teu inimigo na tua mão, e farás com ele como parecer bom aos teus olhos.'" E Davi se levantou e cortou às escondidas a ponta do manto que [era] de Saul.
pt.B: Os homens de Davi lhe disseram: "Este é o dia de que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} falou quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse ao senhor: 'Vou entregar o teu inimigo nas tuas mãos, e poderás fazer com ele o que achares melhor.'" Então Davi se levantou e, sem fazer barulho, cortou a ponta do manto de Saul.
pt.R: Os homens de Davi cochicharam: "Chegou o dia de que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} falou ao senhor! Foi isto que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: 'Vou entregar o teu inimigo nas tuas mãos. Poderás fazer com ele o que quiseres.'" Davi se levantou e foi chegando perto. Sem que Saul percebesse, ele cortou a ponta do manto de Saul.

decisions.choice: the day of which the LORD said: the men's reading of God's promises
alternatives: a promise given to David that is not recorded elsewhere
decisions.reason: No such word from the LORD is recorded in the earlier chapters. The men may be applying God's choice of David as king (16:1-13) and Jonathan's assurance (23:17) to this moment, or quoting a promise the writer has not told. Either way, they take the chance meeting as a sign that God means David to kill Saul; David's answer in verse 7 says otherwise.

decisions.choice: your enemy (singular)
decisions.reason: The written text can be read "your enemies", but the form the scribes marked to be read aloud is "your enemy", and the rest of the sentence speaks of one man ("do to him"). This translation follows the form read aloud.

decisions.choice: cut off the corner of the robe: an act that touches Saul's kingship
decisions.reason: The corner or hem of a robe could stand for its wearer's authority. When Saul tore the corner of Samuel's robe, Samuel said that the LORD had torn the kingdom from Saul (15:27-28). David's cut is a silent sign of the same thing, and it is why his conscience troubles him in verse 6.

decisions.choice: in secret: without Saul noticing
decisions.reason: The word means quietly or unnoticed (18:22; Ruth 3:7, where Ruth comes quietly to Boaz).

decisions.choice: whatever you think best (Balanced); whatever you want (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Good in your eyes" means what seems right to you. Readable adds "whispered" and "crept close", which the setting implies: the men are hiding in the cave with Saul at the entrance.

decisions.choice: David's men call him "장군님" (commander) in the formal polite style
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has them speak to David without a title; Korean needs one for a leader of armed men, and "장군님" fits his place at the head of his band.

decisions.choice: o senhor (David's men to David); tu (the LORD's words to David)
decisions.reason: David's men speak up to their leader with "o senhor", as a servant to a master (1:15; 14:7), while the LORD's words they quote keep God's "tu" to one person ("o teu inimigo", "farás").

decisions.choice: a ponta do manto
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also verses 6 and 12): "ponta" names the corner or edge of the garment that could stand for its wearer's authority (m3), and "manto" is the word of 2:19 and 15:27, so the link with Samuel's torn robe can be seen. Readable keeps "ponta" too, where the English Readable says "piece" in verse 12.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֔ן וַיַּ֥ךְ לֵב־דָּוִ֖ד אֹת֑וֹ עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֔ת אֶת־כָּנָ֖ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְשָׁאֽוּל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was after thus, and struck [the] heart of David him because he had cut off [the] corner which [belonged] to Saul.

en.L: And it happened afterward that David's heart struck him because he had cut off the corner that belonged to Saul.
en.B: Afterward David's conscience troubled him because he had cut off the corner of Saul's robe.
en.R: But afterward David felt guilty for cutting off the corner of Saul's robe.

es.L: Y sucedió después de esto que el corazón de David lo golpeó, porque había cortado la orilla que era de Saúl.
es.B: Después a David le remordió la conciencia por haber cortado la orilla del manto de Saúl.
es.R: Pero después David se sintió culpable por haber cortado un pedazo del manto de Saúl.

fr.L: Et il arriva, après cela, que le cœur de David le frappa, parce qu’il avait coupé le pan qui appartenait à Saül.
fr.B: Ensuite, David eut mauvaise conscience d’avoir coupé le pan du manteau de Saül.
fr.R: Mais après, David s’est senti coupable d’avoir coupé un morceau du manteau de Saül.

sw.L: Ikawa baadaye moyo wa Daudi ukampiga, kwa sababu alikuwa amekata pindo la [joho la] Sauli.
sw.B: Baadaye dhamiri ya Daudi ikamsumbua kwa sababu alikuwa amekata pindo la joho la Sauli.
sw.R: Lakini baadaye Daudi akajisikia kuwa na hatia kwa kukata pindo la joho la Sauli.

vi.L: Sau đó, lòng Đa-vít tự trách ông vì đã cắt vạt [áo] của Sau-lơ.
vi.B: Sau đó lương tâm Đa-vít cắn rứt vì ông đã cắt vạt áo choàng của Sau-lơ.
vi.R: Nhưng sau đó Đa-vít cảm thấy có lỗi vì đã cắt vạt áo choàng của Sau-lơ.

ko.L: 그리고 그 뒤에 다윗의 마음이 그를 쳤다. 그가 사울의 옷자락을 잘랐기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 다윗은 사울의 겉옷 자락을 자른 일로 양심의 가책을 느꼈다.
ko.R: 그러나 나중에 다윗은 사울의 겉옷 자락을 자른 것 때문에 마음이 몹시 괴로웠다.

pt.L: E aconteceu depois disso que o coração de Davi o golpeou, porque ele tinha cortado a ponta que [era] de Saul.
pt.B: Depois disso a consciência de Davi o acusou, porque ele tinha cortado a ponta do manto de Saul.
pt.R: Mas depois Davi se sentiu culpado por ter cortado a ponta do manto de Saul.

decisions.choice: his heart struck him: his conscience troubled him
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and conscience. The same words are used when David's heart strikes him after he counts the people (2 Samuel 24:10). Even this small act against the king felt to David like an attack on the man the LORD had chosen (verse 7).

decisions.choice: conscience
decisions.reason: Balanced says "conscience" for the heart in this sense; Readable says that David "felt guilty". Both add "robe", which the Hebrew leaves to be understood from verse 5.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו חָלִ֧ילָה לִּ֣י מֵֽיהוָ֗ה אִם־אֶעֱשֶׂה֩ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֨ר הַזֶּ֤ה לַֽאדֹנִי֙ לִמְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה לִשְׁלֹ֥חַ יָדִ֖י בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to his men, Far be it to me from [the] LORD that I should do this thing to my lord, to [the] anointed of [the] LORD, to stretch out my hand against him, for [the] anointed of [the] LORD [is] he.

en.L: And he said to his men, "Far be it from me, by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that I should do this thing to my lord, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, for he is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed."
en.B: He told his men, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} forbid that I do this to my lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed, and raise my hand against him! He is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed."
en.R: He said to his men, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keep me from doing such a thing to my master! He is the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed. I must never attack him, because he is the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed."

es.L: Y dijo a sus hombres: «Lejos esté de mí, por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que yo haga tal cosa a mi señor, al ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, extendiendo mi mano contra él, porque él es el ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.B: Les dijo a sus hombres: «¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me libre de hacerle esto a mi señor, el ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y de levantar la mano contra él! Él es el ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.R: Les dijo a sus hombres: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me guarde de hacerle algo así a mi señor! Él es el rey que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha ungido. Nunca debo atacarlo, porque es el rey que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha ungido».

fr.L: Et il dit à ses hommes : « Loin de moi, de par {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, que je fasse cette chose à mon seigneur, à l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, en étendant ma main contre lui, car il [est] l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »
fr.B: Il dit à ses hommes : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me garde de faire une chose pareille à mon seigneur, l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et de lever la main sur lui ! Car il est l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: Il a dit à ses hommes : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’empêche de faire une chose pareille à mon maître ! C’est le roi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a oint. Je ne dois jamais l’attaquer, parce que c’est le roi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a oint. »

sw.L: Akawaambia watu wake, "Hasha kwangu mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nisifanye jambo hili kwa bwana wangu, masihi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kunyosha mkono wangu juu yake, kwa maana yeye ni masihi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.B: Akawaambia watu wake, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} apishe mbali nisimtendee bwana wangu jambo hili, yeye mfalme wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyempaka mafuta, na kuinua mkono wangu juu yake! Yeye ni mfalme wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyempaka mafuta."
sw.R: Akawaambia watu wake, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na anizuie nisimtendee bwana wangu jambo kama hilo! Yeye ni mfalme ambaye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amempaka mafuta. Kamwe nisimshambulie, kwa sababu yeye ni mfalme ambaye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amempaka mafuta."

vi.L: Ông nói với những người của mình: "Nhân danh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, tôi không bao giờ làm điều này cho chúa tôi, là người được xức dầu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, mà giơ tay hại người, vì người là người được xức dầu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."
vi.B: Ông bảo thuộc hạ: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ngăn tôi đừng làm điều ấy cho chúa tôi, là vị vua được {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xức dầu, mà giơ tay hại người! Vì người là vị vua được {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xức dầu."
vi.R: Ông nói với thuộc hạ: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giữ tôi khỏi làm điều như vậy cho chủ tôi! Người là vị vua {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã xức dầu. Tôi không bao giờ được tấn công người, vì người là vị vua {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã xức dầu."

ko.L: 그리고 그가 그의 부하들에게 말했다. "내가 내 주, 곧 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 기름 부음 받은 이에게 이런 일을 하여 그에게 내 손을 대는 것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 절대로 있을 수 없는 일이다. 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 기름 부음 받은 이이기 때문이다."
ko.B: 다윗이 부하들에게 말했다. "내가 내 주인, 곧 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 기름 부으신 이에게 이런 일을 하여 그에게 손을 대는 일은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 금하신다! 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 기름 부으신 이이다."
ko.R: 다윗이 부하들에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내가 내 주인에게 그런 일을 하지 못하게 막아 주시기를 바란다! 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 기름 부어 세우신 왕이다. 나는 절대로 그를 공격해서는 안 된다. 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 기름 부어 세우신 왕이기 때문이다."

pt.L: E ele disse aos seus homens: "Longe de mim, {{divine_name:pelo SENHOR|por Javé}}, que eu faça esta coisa ao meu senhor, ao ungido {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, estendendo a minha mão contra ele, porque ele é o ungido {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}."
pt.B: Ele disse aos seus homens: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} me livre de fazer isso ao meu senhor, o ungido {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e estender a mão contra ele! Ele é o ungido {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}."
pt.R: Ele disse aos seus homens: "Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me livre de fazer uma coisa dessas ao meu senhor! Ele é o rei que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} ungiu. Nunca vou atacá-lo, porque ele é o rei que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} ungiu."

decisions.choice: the LORD's anointed: the king whom the LORD chose and set apart by anointing
decisions.reason: Saul was anointed with oil by Samuel at the LORD's command (10:1), and the oil marked him as the LORD's own choice to rule. The phrase names the king by his relation to God: to raise a hand against him is to strike at the One who appointed him. David holds to this here, again in verse 11 and in 26:9-11, 23, and he treats the man who claims to have killed Saul as guilty for it (2 Samuel 1:14-16). The word is *mashiach*, "anointed one", the word that later became a title for the promised king (Psalm 2:2).

decisions.choice: far be it from me from the LORD: an oath-like refusal
decisions.reason: The first word is a strong exclamation, "profane!" or "unthinkable!" (Genesis 18:25). Adding "from the LORD" makes it a solemn refusal before God, close to "the LORD forbid" (26:11; 1 Kings 21:3).

decisions.choice: stretch out my hand against: attack, do harm to
decisions.reason: To stretch out the hand against someone is to attack them (22:17; 26:9).

decisions.choice: the king the LORD has anointed
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "the LORD's anointed". "Anointed" on its own is not an everyday word, and a reader may not know that it means the king, so Readable says "the king the LORD has anointed" each time the phrase comes in these books. This is the one wording used for the phrase throughout Samuel, Kings and Chronicles at Readable.

decisions.choice: the LORD forbid (Balanced); May the LORD keep me from (Readable); my master (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a familiar form of the oath-like refusal. Readable says "master" for "my lord", because David is speaking of the king he served, and "lord" could be confused with the LORD.

decisions.choice: l'oint du SEIGNEUR (L, B); le roi que le SEIGNEUR a oint (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for *mashiaḥ YHWH*, following the English (r-en-1): "oint" is not an everyday word, so Readable says who is meant. The span takes in the contracted article ("{{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}").

decisions.choice: el ungido del SEÑOR (L, B); el rey que el SEÑOR ha ungido (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for *mashiaḥ YHWH* (m1, r-en-1): the king the LORD chose and set apart by anointing. Readable says so in plain words. Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: "masihi wa BWANA" (L); "mfalme wa BWANA aliyempaka mafuta" (B); "mfalme ambaye BWANA amempaka mafuta" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note for *mashiaḥ YHWH* in these books. "Masihi" is the Hebrew title itself; Balanced and Readable say who he is, so that readers do not take "Masihi" as the later title of Christ.

decisions.choice: "người được xức dầu của CHÚA" (L); "vị vua được CHÚA xức dầu" (B); "vị vua CHÚA đã xức dầu" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note for *mashiaḥ YHWH*; this holds through the block (26:9-23).

decisions.choice: David calls Saul "chúa tôi" (L, B) and "chủ tôi" (R) when he speaks of him to his men
decisions.reason: "my lord" spoken about the king, not to him; Readable "chủ tôi" follows the English "my master".

decisions.choice: "주의 기름 부음 받은 이" (L); "주께서 기름 부으신 이" (B); "주께서 기름 부어 세우신 왕" (R) for *mashiaḥ YHWH*
decisions.reason: The forms the terms of this translation set for 1 and 2 Samuel; Readable says plainly that it is the king, as the English Readable does from this verse on.

decisions.choice: David speaks to his men in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: As with David and his men from 23:3.

decisions.choice: o ungido do SENHOR (L, B); o rei que o SENHOR ungiu (R); estender a mão contra
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also verse 11; 26:9, 11, 16, 23): "o ungido do SENHOR" as 2:10 settled, and David's refusal keeps one wording per level wherever it recurs: "Não estenderei a minha mão contra o meu senhor, porque ele é o ungido do SENHOR" (L), "Não estenderei a mão contra o meu senhor, porque ele é o ungido do SENHOR" (B), "Não vou atacar o meu senhor, porque ele é o rei que o SENHOR ungiu" (R).

decisions.choice: o meu senhor
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "senhor" for the king, where the English Readable says "master": in Portuguese "meu senhor" is the everyday word for one's master, and the capitals of "SENHOR" set the LORD apart in writing; "amo" is archaic and "mestre" means a teacher.

source.text: וַיְשַׁסַּ֨ע דָּוִ֤ד אֶת־אֲנָשָׁיו֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א נְתָנָ֖ם לָק֣וּם אֶל־שָׁא֑וּל וְשָׁא֛וּל קָ֥ם מֵהַמְּעָרָ֖ה וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And restrained David his men with words and not he permitted them to rise against Saul. And Saul arose from the cave and went on [his] way.

en.L: And David held back his men with [these] words, and did not permit them to rise against Saul. And Saul rose up from the cave and went on [his] way.
en.B: With these words David held his men back and would not let them attack Saul. Saul got up, left the cave and went on his way.
en.R: David spoke firmly to his men and did not let them attack Saul. Then Saul got up, left the cave and went on his way.

es.L: Y contuvo David a sus hombres con [estas] palabras, y no les permitió levantarse contra Saúl. Y Saúl se levantó de la cueva y siguió [su] camino.
es.B: Con estas palabras David contuvo a sus hombres y no los dejó atacar a Saúl. Saúl se levantó, salió de la cueva y siguió su camino.
es.R: David les habló con firmeza a sus hombres y no los dejó atacar a Saúl. Luego Saúl se levantó, salió de la cueva y siguió su camino.

fr.L: Et David retint ses hommes par [ces] paroles, et il ne leur permit pas de se lever contre Saül. Et Saül se leva [et sortit] de la grotte, et il alla son chemin.
fr.B: Par ces paroles, David retint ses hommes et ne les laissa pas attaquer Saül. Saül se leva, sortit de la grotte et poursuivit son chemin.
fr.R: David a parlé fermement à ses hommes et il ne les a pas laissés attaquer Saül. Ensuite, Saül s’est levé, il est sorti de la grotte et il a continué son chemin.

sw.L: Daudi akawazuia watu wake kwa [maneno haya], wala hakuwaruhusu wainuke juu ya Sauli. Sauli akainuka kutoka pangoni, akaenda zake njiani.
sw.B: Kwa maneno hayo Daudi akawazuia watu wake, wala hakuwaruhusu wamshambulie Sauli. Sauli akainuka, akatoka pangoni, akaenda zake.
sw.R: Daudi akawaonya watu wake kwa maneno makali, wala hakuwaruhusu wamshambulie Sauli. Kisha Sauli akainuka, akatoka pangoni, akaenda zake.

vi.L: Đa-vít dùng [những] lời ấy cản những người của mình lại, không cho họ nổi lên chống lại Sau-lơ. Sau-lơ đứng dậy ra khỏi hang và đi [đường mình].
vi.B: Với những lời ấy, Đa-vít ngăn thuộc hạ lại và không cho họ tấn công Sau-lơ. Sau-lơ đứng dậy ra khỏi hang và tiếp tục lên đường.
vi.R: Đa-vít nghiêm khắc nói với thuộc hạ và không cho họ tấn công Sau-lơ. Rồi Sau-lơ đứng dậy, ra khỏi hang và tiếp tục đi.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 이 말로 그의 부하들을 막아, 그들이 사울을 치려고 일어나지 못하게 했다. 그리고 사울은 굴에서 일어나 길을 갔다.
ko.B: 다윗은 이 말로 부하들을 말려, 그들이 사울을 공격하지 못하게 했다. 사울은 일어나 굴을 나가서 자기 길을 갔다.
ko.R: 다윗은 부하들을 엄하게 꾸짖고, 그들이 사울을 공격하지 못하게 했다. 사울은 일어나 굴에서 나와 자기 길을 갔다.

pt.L: E Davi conteve os seus homens com [estas] palavras, e não lhes permitiu levantar-se contra Saul. E Saul se levantou da caverna e seguiu o [seu] caminho.
pt.B: Com essas palavras Davi conteve os seus homens e não deixou que atacassem Saul. Saul se levantou, saiu da caverna e seguiu o seu caminho.
pt.R: Davi falou duro com os seus homens e não deixou que eles atacassem Saul. Depois Saul se levantou, saiu da caverna e seguiu o seu caminho.

decisions.choice: restrained: checked them sharply
decisions.reason: The verb elsewhere means to tear apart (Judges 14:6, of Samson tearing the lion). Used of words, it means David cut his men short and held them back with a firm rebuke.

decisions.choice: rise against Saul: attack him
decisions.reason: To rise against someone is to attack (Deuteronomy 19:11; 22:26).

decisions.choice: held back (Balanced); spoke firmly to (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both levels keep the force of the verb: David did not merely advise his men but stopped them with what he said.

source.text: וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֜ד אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן וַיֵּצֵא֙ מֵֽהַמְּעָרָ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֧א אַֽחֲרֵי־שָׁא֛וּל לֵאמֹ֖ר אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּבֵּ֤ט שָׁאוּל֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וַיִּקֹּ֨ד דָּוִ֥ד אַפַּ֛יִם אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And arose David after thus and went out from the cave and called after Saul, saying, My lord the king! And looked Saul behind him, and bowed David face to [the] ground and prostrated himself.

en.L: And David arose afterward and went out of the cave and called after Saul, saying, "My lord the king!" And Saul looked behind him, and David bowed his face to the ground and prostrated himself.
en.B: Afterward David also got up, went out of the cave and called after Saul, "My lord the king!" Saul looked back, and David bowed low with his face to the ground and lay prostrate before him.
en.R: After that, David also came out of the cave. He called after Saul, "My lord the king!" Saul turned to look, and David bowed down low with his face to the ground.

es.L: Y se levantó David después de esto, y salió de la cueva y gritó tras Saúl, diciendo: «¡Mi señor el rey!». Y miró Saúl tras de sí, y David inclinó su rostro a tierra y se postró.
es.B: Después David también se levantó, salió de la cueva y le gritó a Saúl: «¡Mi señor el rey!». Saúl miró hacia atrás, y David se inclinó rostro en tierra y se postró ante él.
es.R: Después de eso, David también salió de la cueva. Le gritó a Saúl: «¡Mi señor el rey!». Saúl se volvió para mirar, y David se inclinó hasta tocar el suelo con la cara.

fr.L: Et David se leva ensuite, et il sortit de la grotte et cria derrière Saül, en disant : « Mon seigneur le roi ! » Et Saül regarda derrière lui, et David s’inclina le visage contre terre et se prosterna.
fr.B: Ensuite David se leva à son tour, sortit de la grotte et cria derrière Saül : « Mon seigneur le roi ! » Saül se retourna, et David s’inclina le visage contre terre et se prosterna devant lui.
fr.R: Après cela, David est sorti lui aussi de la grotte. Il a crié derrière Saül : « Mon seigneur le roi ! » Saül s’est retourné, et David s’est incliné très bas, le visage contre terre.

sw.L: Baadaye Daudi akainuka, akatoka pangoni, akamwita Sauli kwa sauti nyuma yake, akisema, "Bwana wangu mfalme!" Sauli akatazama nyuma yake, naye Daudi akainama uso wake hadi chini, akasujudu.
sw.B: Baadaye Daudi naye akainuka, akatoka pangoni, akamwita Sauli kwa sauti, "Bwana wangu mfalme!" Sauli alipotazama nyuma, Daudi akainama uso wake hadi chini, akasujudu mbele yake.
sw.R: Baada ya hapo, Daudi naye akatoka pangoni. Akamwita Sauli kwa sauti, "Bwana wangu mfalme!" Sauli akageuka kutazama, naye Daudi akainama sana, uso wake ukigusa ardhi.

vi.L: Sau đó Đa-vít đứng dậy, ra khỏi hang và gọi theo Sau-lơ: "Thưa chúa tôi là vua!" Sau-lơ nhìn lại phía sau, và Đa-vít cúi mặt xuống đất và sấp mình lạy.
vi.B: Sau đó Đa-vít cũng đứng dậy, ra khỏi hang và gọi theo Sau-lơ: "Tâu bệ hạ!" Sau-lơ ngoái lại, và Đa-vít cúi rạp mặt xuống đất, sấp mình lạy vua.
vi.R: Sau đó Đa-vít cũng ra khỏi hang. Ông gọi theo Sau-lơ: "Tâu đức vua!" Sau-lơ quay lại nhìn, và Đa-vít cúi sấp mặt xuống đất.

ko.L: 그리고 그 뒤에 다윗도 일어나 굴에서 나가 사울의 뒤에서 외쳐 말했다. "내 주 임금님!" 그러자 사울이 뒤를 돌아보았고, 다윗은 얼굴을 땅에 대고 절했다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 다윗도 일어나 굴에서 나가 사울의 뒤에다 대고 외쳤다. "내 주 임금님!" 사울이 뒤를 돌아보자, 다윗은 얼굴을 땅에 대고 엎드려 절했다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 다윗도 굴에서 나왔다. 그는 사울의 뒤에서 외쳤다. "내 주 임금님!" 사울이 뒤를 돌아보자, 다윗은 얼굴을 땅에 대고 깊이 절했다.

pt.L: E Davi se levantou depois disso, e saiu da caverna, e chamou atrás de Saul, dizendo: "Meu senhor, o rei!" E Saul olhou para trás, e Davi inclinou o rosto em terra e se prostrou.
pt.B: Depois Davi também se levantou, saiu da caverna e gritou para Saul: "Meu senhor, o rei!" Saul olhou para trás, e Davi se curvou com o rosto em terra e se prostrou diante dele.
pt.R: Depois disso Davi também saiu da caverna. Ele gritou para Saul: "Meu senhor, o rei!" Saul se virou para olhar, e Davi se curvou bem baixo, com o rosto no chão.

decisions.choice: from the cave: a spelling difference only
decisions.reason: The written text and the form the scribes marked to be read aloud spell "from the cave" slightly differently. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: bowed his face to the ground and prostrated himself: full homage to the king
decisions.reason: Two verbs describe one act of deep respect: bending low and then lying face down (Genesis 43:28; 1 Kings 1:31). David, whom Saul is hunting, still honors him as his king and lord.

decisions.choice: My lord the king
decisions.reason: All levels keep "lord" here, since this is the way a subject addressed a king; Readable keeps it because it is a cry of address, not a description as in verse 7.

decisions.choice: Mon seigneur le roi
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets: the subject's address to the king is "mon seigneur le roi" at every level, as the English keeps "lord" (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: mi señor el rey
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note's wording at every level (r-en-1); with tú, it carries the respect a subject owes the king. Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: "Bwana wangu mfalme"
decisions.reason: As the terms note, at every level: the usual way a subject addresses the king.

decisions.choice: "chúa tôi là vua" (L); "bệ hạ" (B); "đức vua" (R) for "my lord the king"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for "my lord the king".

decisions.choice: "내 주 임금님" for "My lord the king"
decisions.reason: The form the terms of this translation set; David speaks to Saul in the formal polite style.

decisions.choice: Meu senhor, o rei; o senhor (David to Saul, verses 10-16)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 26:17-20): David speaks to Saul as a subject to his king, with "meu senhor, o rei", "o senhor" and, where the Hebrew has it, "o seu servo" (17:32); Saul answers him with "você" and "meu filho Davi" (verse 17).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ לְשָׁא֔וּל לָ֧מָּה תִשְׁמַ֛ע אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י אָדָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ רָעָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Saul, Why do you listen to [the] words of man, saying, Look, David [is] seeking your harm?

en.L: And David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to the words of {{gender:people|men}} who say, 'Look, David seeks your harm'?
en.B: David said to Saul, "Why do you listen when {{gender:people|men}} say, 'David is out to harm you'?
en.R: David said to Saul, "Why do you believe {{gender:people|men}} who tell you, 'David wants to hurt you'?

es.L: Y dijo David a Saúl: «¿Por qué escuchas las palabras de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} que dicen: “He aquí que David busca tu mal”?
es.B: David le dijo a Saúl: «¿Por qué haces caso cuando {{gender:la gente dice|los hombres dicen}}: “David quiere hacerte daño”?
es.R: David le dijo a Saúl: «¿Por qué crees {{gender:a la gente que te dice|a los hombres que te dicen}}: “David te quiere hacer daño”?

fr.L: Et David dit à Saül : « Pourquoi écoutes-tu les paroles {{gender:des gens|des hommes}} qui disent : “Voici, David cherche ton malheur” ?
fr.B: David dit à Saül : « Pourquoi écoutes-tu {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} qui disent : “David cherche à te nuire” ?
fr.R: David a dit à Saül : « Pourquoi est-ce que tu crois {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} qui te disent : “David veut te faire du mal” ?

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia Sauli, "Kwa nini unasikiliza maneno ya watu wanaosema, 'Tazama, Daudi anatafuta kukudhuru'?
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia Sauli, "Kwa nini unawasikiliza watu wanaposema, 'Daudi anataka kukudhuru'?
sw.R: Daudi akamwambia Sauli, "Kwa nini unawaamini watu wanaokuambia, 'Daudi anataka kukuumiza'?

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với Sau-lơ: "Tại sao vua nghe lời người ta nói rằng: 'Kìa, Đa-vít tìm hại vua'?
vi.B: Đa-vít thưa với Sau-lơ: "Tại sao bệ hạ nghe người ta nói: 'Đa-vít đang tìm cách hại bệ hạ'?
vi.R: Đa-vít thưa với Sau-lơ: "Tại sao đức vua tin những người nói với vua rằng: 'Đa-vít muốn hại vua'?

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 사울에게 말했다. "어찌하여 '보십시오, 다윗이 임금님을 해치려고 합니다' 하고 말하는 사람들의 말을 들으십니까?
ko.B: 다윗이 사울에게 말했다. "어찌하여 임금님께서는 '다윗이 임금님을 해치려고 합니다' 하고 말하는 사람들의 말에 귀를 기울이십니까?
ko.R: 다윗이 사울에게 말했다. "왜 '다윗이 임금님을 해치려고 합니다' 하고 말하는 사람들의 말을 믿으십니까?

pt.L: E Davi disse a Saul: "Por que o senhor ouve as palavras {{gender:das pessoas|dos homens}} que dizem: 'Eis que Davi procura o seu mal'?
pt.B: Davi disse a Saul: "Por que o senhor dá ouvidos quando {{gender:as pessoas|os homens}} dizem: 'Davi quer fazer mal ao senhor'?
pt.R: Davi disse a Saul: "Por que o senhor acredita {{gender:nas pessoas|nos homens}} que lhe dizem: 'Davi quer fazer mal ao senhor'?

decisions.choice: man: people in general
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being, used here of people as a group. David does not name anyone; he lays the blame on the talk around Saul rather than on Saul himself. Saul had complained that no one told him the truth about David (22:8), and informers had been bringing him reports (23:19).

decisions.choice: seeking your harm: trying to do you evil
decisions.reason: The word means harm or evil. The charge is that David is plotting against the king's life, the charge Saul made in 22:8, 13.

decisions.choice: people (default); men (alternative)
decisions.reason: The word means people of either sex, so every level uses the gender setting. Readable says "believe" for "listen to", since Saul has acted on what he heard.

decisions.choice: {{gender:les gens|les hommes}}
decisions.reason: The word means people of either sex (m1); as the English, the inclusive word is the default and the traditional "les hommes" the alternative, with the article inside the span.

decisions.choice: {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew means people in general (m1). Spanish has two wordings, as the English has (r-en-1): “la gente” by default, “los hombres” as the alternative; the span takes in the verb where it agrees.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "người ta"
decisions.reason: "người ta" is people of either sex, so Vietnamese has one wording (as at 16:7).

decisions.choice: "사람들" (people), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "사람들" already includes everyone (meaning decision m1); there is no second wording for the setting to offer.

source.text: הִנֵּה֩ הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה רָא֣וּ עֵינֶ֗יךָ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־נְתָנְךָ֩ יְהוָ֨ה׀הַיּ֤וֹם׀בְּיָדִי֙ בַּמְּעָרָ֔ה וְאָמַ֥ר לַהֲרָגֲךָ֖ וַתָּ֣חָס עָלֶ֑יךָ וָאֹמַ֗ר לֹא־אֶשְׁלַ֤ח יָדִי֙ בַּֽאדֹנִ֔י כִּי־מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, this day have seen your eyes how gave you [the] LORD today into my hand in the cave. And [one] said to kill you, but it spared you, and I said, Not I will stretch out my hand against my lord, for [the] anointed of [the] LORD [is] he.

en.L: Look, this day your eyes have seen how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave you today into my hand in the cave. And [someone] said to kill you, but [my eye] spared you, and I said, 'I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed.'
en.B: Today you have seen with your own eyes how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put you into my hands in the cave. I was urged to kill you, but I spared you. I said, 'I will not raise my hand against my lord, because he is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed.'
en.R: Today you have seen for yourself that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put you in my power in that cave. Some of my men told me to kill you, but I would not. I said, 'I will not attack my master, because he is the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed.'

es.L: He aquí que este día han visto tus ojos cómo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te puso hoy en mi mano en la cueva. Y [alguien] dijo que te matara, pero [mi ojo] te perdonó, y dije: “No extenderé mi mano contra mi señor, porque él es el ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}”.
es.B: Hoy has visto con tus propios ojos cómo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te puso en mis manos en la cueva. Me insistieron en que te matara, pero te perdoné la vida. Dije: “No levantaré la mano contra mi señor, porque él es el ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}”.
es.R: Hoy has visto por ti mismo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te puso en mi poder en esa cueva. Algunos de mis hombres me dijeron que te matara, pero no quise. Dije: “No atacaré a mi señor, porque es el rey que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha ungido”.

fr.L: Voici, en ce jour, tes yeux ont vu comment {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a livré aujourd’hui dans ma main, dans la grotte. Et [on m’]a dit de te tuer, mais [mon œil] t’a épargné, et j’ai dit : “Je n’étendrai pas la main contre mon seigneur, car il [est] l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.”
fr.B: Aujourd’hui, tu as vu de tes propres yeux comment {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a livré entre mes mains dans la grotte. On m’a poussé à te tuer, mais je t’ai épargné. J’ai dit : “Je ne lèverai pas la main sur mon seigneur, car il est l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.”
fr.R: Aujourd’hui, tu as vu toi-même que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’avait mis en mon pouvoir dans cette grotte. Certains de mes hommes m’ont dit de te tuer, mais je ne l’ai pas fait. J’ai dit : “Je n’attaquerai pas mon maître, parce que c’est le roi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a oint.”

sw.L: Tazama, siku hii ya leo macho yako yameona jinsi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokutia leo mkononi mwangu pangoni. [Mtu] akasema nikuue, lakini [jicho langu] likakuhurumia, nikasema, 'Sitanyosha mkono wangu juu ya bwana wangu, kwa maana yeye ni masihi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.'
sw.B: Leo umeona kwa macho yako mwenyewe jinsi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokutia mikononi mwangu pangoni. Nilihimizwa nikuue, lakini nilikuhurumia. Nilisema, 'Sitainua mkono wangu juu ya bwana wangu, kwa sababu yeye ni mfalme wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyempaka mafuta.'
sw.R: Leo umejionea mwenyewe kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikutia katika uwezo wangu ndani ya pango lile. Baadhi ya watu wangu waliniambia nikuue, lakini sikukubali. Nilisema, 'Sitamshambulia bwana wangu, kwa sababu yeye ni mfalme ambaye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amempaka mafuta.'

vi.L: Kìa, ngày nay mắt vua đã thấy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phó vua vào tay tôi trong hang hôm nay thế nào. [Có người] bảo giết vua, nhưng [mắt tôi] đã tha cho vua, và tôi nói: 'Tôi sẽ không giơ tay hại chúa tôi, vì người là người được xức dầu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.'
vi.B: Hôm nay chính mắt bệ hạ đã thấy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phó bệ hạ vào tay tôi trong hang thế nào. Có người giục tôi giết bệ hạ, nhưng tôi đã tha. Tôi nói: 'Tôi sẽ không giơ tay hại chúa tôi, vì người là vị vua được {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xức dầu.'
vi.R: Hôm nay đức vua đã tận mắt thấy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đặt vua vào tay tôi trong cái hang đó. Có mấy người của tôi bảo tôi giết vua, nhưng tôi không làm. Tôi nói: 'Tôi sẽ không tấn công chủ tôi, vì người là vị vua {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã xức dầu.'

ko.L: 보십시오, 오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 굴에서 임금님을 제 손에 넘겨주신 것을 오늘 임금님의 눈으로 보셨습니다. 그리고 [누군가] 임금님을 죽이라고 말했지만, [제 눈이] 임금님을 아꼈습니다. 그래서 저는 '내 주께 내 손을 대지 않겠다. 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 기름 부음 받은 이이다' 하고 말했습니다.
ko.B: 오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 굴 속에서 임금님을 제 손에 넘겨주신 것을 임금님께서도 직접 보셨습니다. 저더러 임금님을 죽이라는 사람도 있었지만, 저는 임금님을 살려 드렸습니다. 저는 '내 주께 손을 대지 않겠다. 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 기름 부으신 이이다' 하고 말했습니다.
ko.R: 오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 굴에서 임금님을 제 손에 넘겨주신 것을 임금님께서도 보셨습니다. 제 부하들 가운데 몇이 저에게 임금님을 죽이라고 했지만, 저는 그렇게 하지 않았습니다. 저는 '내 주인을 공격하지 않겠다. 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 기름 부어 세우신 왕이다' 하고 말했습니다.

pt.L: Eis que neste dia os seus olhos viram como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} hoje o entregou na minha mão, na caverna. E [alguém] disse para matá-lo, mas [o meu olho] o poupou, e eu disse: 'Não estenderei a minha mão contra o meu senhor, porque ele é o ungido {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.'
pt.B: Hoje o senhor viu com os próprios olhos como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} o entregou nas minhas mãos, na caverna. Insistiram comigo para que eu o matasse, mas eu o poupei. Eu disse: 'Não estenderei a mão contra o meu senhor, porque ele é o ungido {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.'
pt.R: Hoje o senhor viu com os próprios olhos que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} o colocou em meu poder naquela caverna. Alguns dos meus homens me disseram para matá-lo, mas eu não quis. Eu disse: 'Não vou atacar o meu senhor, porque ele é o rei que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} ungiu.'

decisions.choice: and one said to kill you: I was urged to kill you
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject: "someone said", that is, it was said. It points back to David's men urging him in verse 5.

decisions.choice: it spared you: my eye had pity on you, I spared you
decisions.reason: The verb "spare" or "pity" has a feminine subject that is not stated. In this verb's idiom the eye is the one that pities or spares (Deuteronomy 7:16; Ezekiel 7:4), so the sense is "my eye spared you", that is, I spared you. Some old translations read the verb as "I spared"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the LORD's anointed
decisions.reason: As in verse 7: the king whom the LORD chose and set apart. David repeats to Saul the very words he said to his men.

decisions.choice: I was urged (Balanced); Some of my men told me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the impersonal "one said" into a passive. Readable names the speakers from verse 5, where it is David's men who urge him. Readable says "in my power" for "into my hand" and "master" and "the king the LORD has anointed" as in verse 7.

source.text: וְאָבִ֣י רְאֵ֔ה גַּ֗ם רְאֵ֛ה אֶת־כְּנַ֥ף מְעִילְךָ֖ בְּיָדִ֑י כִּ֡י בְּכָרְתִי֩ אֶת־כְּנַ֨ף מְעִֽילְךָ֜ וְלֹ֣א הֲרַגְתִּ֗יךָ דַּ֤ע וּרְאֵה֙ כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין בְּיָדִ֜י רָעָ֤ה וָפֶ֨שַׁע֙ וְלֹא־חָטָ֣אתִי לָ֔ךְ וְאַתָּ֛ה צֹדֶ֥ה אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֖י לְקַחְתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And my father, see, yes, see [the] corner of your robe in my hand, for in my cutting off [the] corner of your robe and not I killed you, know and see that there is not in my hand evil or rebellion, and not I have sinned against you, but you [are] hunting my life to take it.

en.L: And my father, see, yes, see the corner of your robe in my hand. For when I cut off the corner of your robe, I did not kill you. Know and see that there is no evil or rebellion in my hand, and I have not sinned against you, yet you are hunting my life to take it.
en.B: My father, look! See the corner of your robe here in my hand! I cut off the corner of your robe, but I did not kill you. You can know for certain from this that I mean you no harm and am not rebelling against you. I have not wronged you, yet you are hunting me down to take my life.
en.R: My father, look! See this piece of your robe in my hand? I cut it off, but I did not kill you. This proves that I am not trying to hurt you or turn against you. I have done nothing wrong to you, but you are hunting me down to kill me.

es.L: Y padre mío, mira, sí, mira la orilla de tu manto en mi mano; porque cuando corté la orilla de tu manto, no te maté. Sabe y ve que no hay en mi mano mal ni rebelión, y no he pecado contra ti; pero tú andas a la caza de mi vida para quitármela.
es.B: Padre mío, ¡mira! ¡Mira la orilla de tu manto aquí en mi mano! Corté la orilla de tu manto, pero no te maté. Por esto puedes saber con certeza que no te quiero hacer daño ni me estoy rebelando contra ti. No te he hecho ningún mal, y sin embargo tú me andas persiguiendo para quitarme la vida.
es.R: Padre mío, ¡mira! ¿Ves este pedazo de tu manto en mi mano? Lo corté, pero no te maté. Esto demuestra que no estoy tratando de hacerte daño ni de ponerme en contra tuya. No te he hecho nada malo, pero tú me andas persiguiendo para matarme.

fr.L: Et mon père, vois, oui, vois le pan de ton manteau dans ma main ; car en coupant le pan de ton manteau, je ne t’ai pas tué. Sache et vois qu’il n’y a dans ma main ni mal ni révolte, et je n’ai pas péché contre toi, et toi, tu fais la chasse à ma vie pour la prendre.
fr.B: Mon père, regarde ! Vois le pan de ton manteau dans ma main ! J’ai coupé le pan de ton manteau, mais je ne t’ai pas tué. Tu peux en être sûr : je ne te veux aucun mal et je ne me révolte pas contre toi. Je n’ai rien fait de mal contre toi, et pourtant tu me traques pour m’ôter la vie.
fr.R: Mon père, regarde ! Tu vois ce morceau de ton manteau dans ma main ? Je l’ai coupé, mais je ne t’ai pas tué. Cela prouve que je ne cherche pas à te faire du mal ni à me révolter contre toi. Je ne t’ai rien fait de mal, mais toi, tu me poursuis pour me tuer.

sw.L: Baba yangu, ona, naam, ona pindo la joho lako mkononi mwangu. Kwa maana nilipokata pindo la joho lako, sikukuua. Jua na uone kwamba hakuna ubaya wala uasi mkononi mwangu, wala sijakutenda dhambi, lakini wewe unaiwinda nafsi yangu ili kuiondoa.
sw.B: Baba yangu, tazama! Tazama pindo la joho lako hapa mkononi mwangu! Nilikata pindo la joho lako, lakini sikukuua. Kwa hili ujue hakika kwamba sina nia ya kukudhuru wala kukuasi. Sijakukosea, lakini wewe unaniwinda ili kuniondolea uhai wangu.
sw.R: Baba yangu, tazama! Unaona kipande hiki cha joho lako mkononi mwangu? Nilikikata, lakini sikukuua. Hii inaonyesha kwamba sitaki kukuumiza wala kukuasi. Sijakukosea chochote, lakini wewe unaniwinda ili uniue.

vi.L: Thưa cha, xin xem, xin xem vạt áo choàng của cha trong tay con. Vì khi con cắt vạt áo choàng của cha, con đã không giết cha. Xin biết và thấy rằng trong tay con không có điều ác hay sự phản loạn, con không phạm tội với cha, thế mà cha lại săn đuổi mạng sống con để lấy đi.
vi.B: Thưa cha, xin cha xem! Xin xem vạt áo choàng của cha đây trong tay con! Con đã cắt vạt áo choàng của cha mà không giết cha. Do đó cha có thể biết chắc rằng con không có ý hại cha, cũng không phản nghịch cha. Con không làm gì sai với cha, thế mà cha lại săn đuổi con để lấy mạng con.
vi.R: Thưa cha, xin cha nhìn xem! Cha có thấy mảnh áo choàng của cha trong tay con không? Con cắt nó ra, nhưng con không giết cha. Điều này chứng tỏ con không tìm cách hại cha hay chống lại cha. Con không làm gì sai với cha, nhưng cha lại săn đuổi con để giết con.

ko.L: 그리고 내 아버지, 보십시오. 제 손에 있는 임금님의 겉옷 자락을 보십시오. 제가 임금님의 겉옷 자락을 자르고도 임금님을 죽이지 않았으니, 제 손에 악이나 반역이 없고, 제가 임금님께 죄를 짓지 않았다는 것을 알고 보십시오. 그러나 임금님께서는 제 목숨을 빼앗으려고 사냥하고 계십니다.
ko.B: 아버지, 보십시오! 제 손에 있는 이 겉옷 자락을 보십시오! 제가 임금님의 겉옷 자락을 잘랐지만 임금님을 죽이지는 않았습니다. 이것으로 제가 임금님을 해치거나 반역할 마음이 없다는 것을 똑똑히 아실 것입니다. 저는 임금님께 잘못한 것이 없는데, 임금님께서는 제 목숨을 빼앗으려고 저를 사냥하듯 쫓고 계십니다.
ko.R: 아버지, 보십시오! 제 손에 있는 이 겉옷 조각이 보이십니까? 제가 이것을 잘랐지만 임금님을 죽이지는 않았습니다. 이것을 보시면 제가 임금님을 해치거나 배반하려고 하지 않는다는 것을 아실 것입니다. 저는 임금님께 아무 잘못도 하지 않았습니다. 그런데 임금님께서는 저를 죽이려고 사냥하듯 쫓고 계십니다.

pt.L: E, meu pai, veja, sim, veja a ponta do seu manto na minha mão. Pois, quando cortei a ponta do seu manto, não o matei. Saiba e veja que não há na minha mão mal nem rebelião, e eu não pequei contra o senhor; mas o senhor está caçando a minha vida para tirá-la.
pt.B: Meu pai, olhe! Veja a ponta do seu manto aqui na minha mão! Eu cortei a ponta do seu manto, mas não matei o senhor. Por isso o senhor pode ter certeza de que não quero lhe fazer mal nem me rebelar contra o senhor. Não lhe fiz nenhum mal, e mesmo assim o senhor me caça para tirar a minha vida.
pt.R: Meu pai, olhe! Está vendo a ponta do seu manto aqui na minha mão? Eu a cortei, mas não matei o senhor. Isso prova que não estou tentando fazer mal ao senhor nem me voltar contra o rei. Não fiz nada de errado contra o senhor, mas o senhor está me caçando para me matar.

decisions.choice: my father: a title of respect, and Saul is also David's father-in-law
decisions.reason: "Father" can address an older man of rank (2 Kings 5:13), and Saul had given his daughter Michal to David as his wife (18:27). David speaks to him as a son, and Saul answers "my son" in verse 17.

decisions.choice: evil or rebellion: harm against the king or a revolt against his rule
decisions.reason: The second word means breaking faith with or rebelling against an authority (1 Kings 12:19). David says that nothing in his hand, that is, nothing in his actions, shows a plan to harm Saul or seize power.

decisions.choice: hunting my life: lying in wait to kill me
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a hunter lying in wait for prey (Exodus 21:13). David uses the same picture of a hunt in 26:20.

decisions.choice: Look ... look (Balanced); look! See ...? (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "see" for emphasis. Balanced keeps the repetition; Readable makes the second a question, which holds the same urgency. Both split the long sentence into several.

decisions.choice: David turns from "vua" and "tôi" to "cha" and "con" where he says "my father", and keeps them to the end of his speech
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note; "my father" is a title of respect, and Saul is also David's father-in-law (m1). Saul answers with "con" in verse 17.

decisions.choice: "아버지" (my father) as David's address, inside his formal polite speech to the king
decisions.reason: "My father" is a title of respect, and Saul is also David's father-in-law (meaning decision m1); Korean "아버지" carries both, while "장인어른" would lose the respect owed to a king.

source.text: יִשְׁפֹּ֤ט יְהוָה֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔ךָ וּנְקָמַ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה מִמֶּ֑ךָּ וְיָדִ֖י לֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶה־בָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: May judge [the] LORD between me and you, and may avenge me [the] LORD on you, but my hand will not be against you.

en.L: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} judge between me and you, and may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} avenge me on you, but my hand will not be against you.
en.B: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} judge between us, and may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} avenge the wrong you have done me. But I will not lift my hand against you.
en.R: Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} decide which of us is right. Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pay you back for what you have done to me. But I will never harm you myself.

es.L: Que juzgue {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entre tú y yo, y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me vengue de ti; pero mi mano no será contra ti.
es.B: Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} juzgue entre nosotros, y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me haga justicia por el mal que me has hecho. Pero yo no levantaré la mano contra ti.
es.R: Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} decida quién de los dos tiene razón. Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te dé tu merecido por lo que me has hecho. Pero yo nunca te haré daño.

fr.L: Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} juge entre moi et toi, et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me venge de toi, mais ma main ne sera pas contre toi.
fr.B: Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} juge entre nous deux, et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} venge le tort que tu m’as fait. Mais je ne lèverai pas la main sur toi.
fr.R: Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} décide qui de nous deux a raison. Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te fasse payer ce que tu m’as fait. Mais moi, je ne te ferai jamais de mal.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na ahukumu kati yangu na wewe, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na anilipizie kisasi juu yako, lakini mkono wangu hautakuwa juu yako.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na ahukumu kati yetu, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na alipize ubaya ulionitendea. Lakini mimi sitainua mkono wangu juu yako.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na aamue ni nani kati yetu aliye na haki. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na akulipe kwa yale uliyonitendea. Lakini mimi mwenyewe sitakudhuru kamwe.

vi.L: Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xét xử giữa con và cha, và nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} báo thù cho con trên cha, nhưng tay con sẽ không chống lại cha.
vi.B: Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xét xử giữa cha và con, và nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} báo trả điều sai trái cha đã làm cho con. Nhưng con sẽ không giơ tay hại cha.
vi.R: Xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phân xử xem ai trong chúng ta là đúng. Xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} báo trả cha về những gì cha đã làm cho con. Nhưng chính con sẽ không bao giờ hại cha.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 저와 임금님 사이를 재판하시고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 임금님께 제 원수를 갚아 주시기를 바랍니다. 그러나 제 손은 임금님을 치지 않을 것입니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리 둘 사이를 판가름하시고, 임금님께서 제게 하신 일을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 갚아 주시기를 바랍니다. 그러나 저는 임금님께 손을 대지 않겠습니다.
ko.R: 우리 가운데 누가 옳은지 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 판단하시기를 바랍니다. 임금님께서 저에게 하신 일을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 갚아 주시기를 바랍니다. 그러나 저는 결코 제 손으로 임금님을 해치지 않겠습니다.

pt.L: Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} julgue entre mim e o senhor, e que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me vingue do senhor; mas a minha mão não será contra o senhor.
pt.B: Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} julgue entre nós dois, e que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me faça justiça pelo mal que o senhor me fez. Mas eu não levantarei a mão contra o senhor.
pt.R: Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} decida qual de nós está certo. Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} castigue o senhor pelo que fez comigo. Mas eu mesmo nunca vou fazer mal ao senhor.

decisions.choice: may the LORD judge and avenge: David leaves justice to God
decisions.reason: David asks God to decide between them and to right the wrong done to him, and he refuses to take that right into his own hands (Deuteronomy 32:35). The same trust is the point of Abigail's words in 25:26, 31-33 and of David's in 26:10.

decisions.choice: my hand will not be against you: I will not harm you
decisions.reason: The hand stands for action and power: David will do Saul no harm himself.

decisions.choice: avenge the wrong you have done me (Balanced); pay you back (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Avenge me on you" means to give David justice by punishing Saul's wrong. Balanced names the wrong to be avenged, and Readable says "pay you back".

source.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֹאמַ֗ר מְשַׁל֙ הַקַּדְמֹנִ֔י מֵרְשָׁעִ֖ים יֵ֣צֵא רֶ֑שַׁע וְיָדִ֖י לֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶה־בָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: As says [the] proverb of the ancient [ones], From wicked [ones] comes out wickedness, but my hand will not be against you.

en.L: As the proverb of the ancients says, 'From the wicked comes forth wickedness,' but my hand will not be against you.
en.B: As the old proverb says, 'Wickedness comes from the wicked.' But my hand will not be against you.
en.R: There is an old saying: 'Evil things come from evil people.' But I will not harm you.

es.L: Como dice el proverbio de los antiguos: “De los malvados sale la maldad”; pero mi mano no será contra ti.
es.B: Como dice el antiguo proverbio: “La maldad sale de los malvados”. Pero mi mano no se levantará contra ti.
es.R: Hay un viejo dicho: “Las cosas malas vienen de la gente mala”. Pero yo no te haré daño.

fr.L: Comme dit le proverbe des anciens : “Des méchants sort la méchanceté”, mais ma main ne sera pas contre toi.
fr.B: Comme le dit le vieux proverbe : “La méchanceté vient des méchants.” Mais ma main ne sera pas contre toi.
fr.R: Il y a un vieux dicton : “Le mal vient des méchants.” Mais moi, je ne te ferai pas de mal.

sw.L: Kama isemavyo methali ya watu wa kale, 'Kwa waovu hutoka uovu,' lakini mkono wangu hautakuwa juu yako.
sw.B: Kama isemavyo methali ya zamani, 'Uovu hutoka kwa waovu.' Lakini mkono wangu hautakuwa juu yako.
sw.R: Kuna msemo wa zamani: 'Mambo maovu hutoka kwa watu waovu.' Lakini mimi sitakudhuru.

vi.L: Như câu châm ngôn của người xưa nói: 'Từ kẻ ác sinh ra điều ác,' nhưng tay con sẽ không chống lại cha.
vi.B: Như câu châm ngôn xưa có nói: 'Điều ác do kẻ ác mà ra.' Nhưng con sẽ không giơ tay hại cha.
vi.R: Có một câu nói xưa: 'Việc ác đến từ người ác.' Nhưng con sẽ không hại cha.

ko.L: 옛사람들의 속담이 말하는 것처럼 '악인에게서 악이 나온다'고 합니다. 그러나 제 손은 임금님을 치지 않을 것입니다.
ko.B: 옛 속담에 '악은 악인에게서 나온다'고 했습니다. 그러나 저는 임금님께 손을 대지 않겠습니다.
ko.R: '나쁜 일은 나쁜 사람에게서 나온다'는 옛말이 있습니다. 그러나 저는 임금님을 해치지 않겠습니다.

pt.L: Como diz o provérbio dos antigos: 'Dos ímpios sai a impiedade'; mas a minha mão não será contra o senhor.
pt.B: Como diz o velho provérbio: 'A maldade vem dos maus.' Mas a minha mão não será contra o senhor.
pt.R: Há um velho ditado: 'Coisas más vêm de gente má.' Mas eu não vou fazer mal ao senhor.

decisions.choice: the proverb of the ancients: an old saying
alternatives: the proverb of the ancient one (singular)
decisions.reason: The word for proverb is used of a short, well-known saying (10:12). "The ancient ones" may mean people of long ago or simply that the saying is old; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: wickedness comes from the wicked, but my hand will not be against you
alternatives: so my hand will not be against you
decisions.reason: The proverb says that evil deeds come from evil people. David applies it to himself: if he were wicked, he would have killed Saul in the cave; since he did not, Saul can see he is not. It may also hint that Saul's own deeds show what he is, and that God will deal with that. The joining word can be read as "but" or "so".

decisions.choice: an old saying; I will not harm you
decisions.reason: Readable says "saying" for "proverb" and gives the meaning of "my hand will not be against you" as in verse 13.

source.text: אַחֲרֵ֨י מִ֤י יָצָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֥י מִ֖י אַתָּ֣ה רֹדֵ֑ף אַֽחֲרֵי֙ כֶּ֣לֶב מֵ֔ת אַחֲרֵ֖י פַּרְעֹ֥שׁ אֶחָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: After whom has come out [the] king of Israel? After whom [are] you pursuing? After a dog dead, after a flea one!

en.L: After whom has the king of Israel come out? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog! After a single flea!
en.B: Whom has the king of Israel come out to chase? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog! A single flea!
en.R: Who is the king of Israel chasing? Who are you running after? I am no more important than a dead dog or a tiny flea!

es.L: ¿Tras quién ha salido el rey de Israel? ¿Tras quién andas persiguiendo? ¡Tras un perro muerto! ¡Tras una pulga!
es.B: ¿A quién ha salido a perseguir el rey de Israel? ¿A quién vas persiguiendo? ¡A un perro muerto! ¡A una simple pulga!
es.R: ¿A quién persigue el rey de Israel? ¿Detrás de quién andas corriendo? ¡Yo no valgo más que un perro muerto o una pulga!

fr.L: Après qui le roi d’Israël est-il sorti ? Après qui cours-tu ? Après un chien mort, après une seule puce !
fr.B: Qui le roi d’Israël est-il sorti chasser ? Qui poursuis-tu ? Un chien mort ! Une simple puce !
fr.R: Qui le roi d’Israël poursuit-il ? Après qui est-ce que tu cours ? Je ne suis pas plus important qu’un chien mort ou qu’une petite puce !

sw.L: Mfalme wa Israeli ametoka kumfuata nani? Unamfuatia nani? Mbwa mfu! Kiroboto mmoja!
sw.B: Mfalme wa Israeli ametoka kumfukuza nani? Unamfuatia nani? Mbwa mfu! Kiroboto mmoja tu!
sw.R: Mfalme wa Israeli anamfukuza nani? Unamkimbiza nani? Mimi si wa maana kuliko mbwa mfu au kiroboto kidogo!
